doc.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998

title: Leaving Mills, the Bob Crosby Bobcats and the OSS
summary: She urged Gil Rodin to form a small band from Crosby men, left Mills, and joined the OSS; small-band records were popular.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Inspired. So was Monk. Same thing. And anyway, after that well there was a period there, in years perhaps, that completed my career because then I went into the Office of Strategic Services, which was America’s spy unit, you know, and we went abroad, and we sent bodies in France and things like that you know. So that followed and that ended that period of mine. But at that time it was nice, because I worked with Mildred [Bailey] and Red [Norvo] a certain amount, but various people. The Crosby band, I’m the one that said to Gil Roden, form a small band out of those guys, those wonderful guys, Eddie Miller and those guys, because Ray [Baduc] was a good drummer and so on. And they did. And I had a card from Bob Haggart this Christmas, which quoted a little paragraph saying, “Bring on the Bobcats and we’ll go into the back hall“ and so on. But it made me laugh. But I left Mills because I didn’t have a free enough hand, and of course my things weren’t making a lot of money, but Johnny’s “Jeep’s Blues” and those things, they were heard from one end of Harlem to the other end. Juke boxes on every block. And of course it was hugely popular you know. The small bands were very popular. And there was one guy left that had a tremendous amount of talent and never really made it and that was Chick Webb. And he was a wonderful little guy, with tremendous ears. The guys in the band used to say no matter who hit what note, and he couldn’t lead, but he always look around and gave the guy a — stared at the guy. Am I running out of time?
